transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I… I’m here because flying has gotten really hard for me. Just the thought of getting on an airplane scares me badly, even though I know it doesn’t really make sense. It feels like my body is convinced the plane is going to fall.
Do you ever have episodes where you feel an intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes?
Yes. It comes on really fast. Even just getting an email about a rural shift where I’d have to fly… my heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I can’t breathe until I close it.
Is your fear limited to flying or do you experience similar fears in other situations?
It’s really flying. Getting on a plane—or even thinking about it now—sets it off. I know it doesn’t make sense, but it feels like the plane is going to fall.
Have you noticed this kind of intense fear happening in any situations other than flying?
No… not really. It’s the flying. Just the idea of getting on a plane now scares me so badly, even though I know it doesn’t make sense. My body just… feels like the plane is going to fall.
Has your fear of flying stopped you from doing things you want or need to do?

Yes. It’s… gotten in the way. I’ve turned down coverage that would’ve meant flying, and that’s cost me money. People at work have started to wonder if they can count on me. I’ve also missed meetings and put off seeing family because of it.
Have you ever had a similar intense fear of any other specific object, situation, or activity besides flying?

No… I don’t think so. It’s really the airplane thing. Just the thought of getting on one now scares me so bad, even though I know it doesn’t make sense. My body just tells me the plane’s going to fall.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of flying?
About seven months, I think. It started after that rough small-plane flight… around when I’d just lost my clinic job.
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with friends or family?
Yeah… somewhat. I’ve put off seeing my family because I’d have to fly, and that’s caused some strain. I don’t really like talking about it much, but it’s there.
Do you avoid flying as much as possible because of this fear?

Yes. I avoid it as much as I can. I’ve canceled clinic coverage, skipped meetings… and I keep putting off seeing my family in Honduras. If I even get myself to the airport, I’m shaking and I need someone with me.
Have you experienced any fear or discomfort when using other forms of transportation, like trains, boats, or buses?
Not really… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed that with buses or trains. It’s mostly the flying.
Are there any other areas of your life, besides work and seeing family, where your fear of flying is causing problems?

Mostly professional things, I guess. I’ve turned down coverage that involved flying, and that’s cost me income… and I think some colleagues wonder if they can count on me. I’ve also missed meetings because of it. And, well, the family thing too, but I know I already mentioned that.
Have you ever had an intense fear of any other specific object, situation, or activity besides flying?
No… not that I can think of. It’s really just flying.
